anomalies.observed: Q1 (P-MOSFET) has its source (Q1.2) on the regulated +5V output net and its drain (Q1.3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. The LTC4412 VIN pin (U6.1) is on USBC_VBUS_IN and its SENSE pin (U6.6) is on +5V, so the ideal-diode FET is oriented with input and output reversed.
anomalies.expected: For an LTC4412 ideal-diode OR, the P-FET source sits on the VIN (input) side and the drain on the load side, with SENSE monitoring the load (output). The spec calls for USB input OR-ing with reverse-current protection.

evidence.quote: USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : ... Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)
USB diode doesn't work, I guess need ideal diode to handle more power? LTC4412 controller and p-ch mosfet. need reverse current protection mostly

anomalies.impact: The P-FET body diode points from the +5V output toward VBUS, so reverse current from the 5V rail back to USB is not blocked, and USB power may not be routed correctly through the FET. This defeats the reverse-current protection the USB power path is meant to provide.

anomalies.observed: Dual LED D30 channel 2 has its anode A2 (D30.4) on ESTOP_OUT, and its cathode K2 (D30.2) goes through R60 back to the same ESTOP_OUT net. Both ends of that LED path sit on one net, so channel 2 cannot conduct. Channel 1 uses the switched LED supply as its anode, as the other status LEDs do.
anomalies.expected: Channel 2 should have its anode on the same switched LED supply as channel 1 (or +3V3), with the series resistor and cathode driven by the e-stop signal, so that the indicator lights when ESTOP_OUT changes state.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)
/LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV : D28.2(A,passive) D29.2(A,passive) D30.3(A1,input) D8.2(A,passive) Q10.1(G,input) R58.2(2,passive) U34.4(Y,output) U7.5(OE,input)

anomalies.impact: The e-stop status indicator for channel 2 never lights, and the LED is effectively bypassed. This removes a diagnostic indication of e-stop state.

anomalies.observed: D2 (LED_RED) has its anode on the open-drain output U27.Y (net Net-(D2-A)) and its cathode through R31 to GND. Every other status LED in the design has its anode on a supply and its cathode on the driver. U27's A input is tied to +5V, so the open-drain output cannot source the current needed to light D2.
anomalies.expected: The LED should be oriented with its anode on the supply side (through a resistor) and its cathode driven by the open-drain output, consistent with the other indicators (e.g. D1, D12, D17, D28, D29).
anomalies.impact: The red indicator D2 is likely never lit, or it is driven in the wrong sense, so the status indication is lost.
